neighbours.label: ' even' opening a concessive 'even if/when' clause that keeps a condition steady or normal, vs the same sentences with a plain 'if/when/because' clause
fire: Sea levels would keep rising even if emissions stopped tomorrow.
The soup stays hot for hours even if you leave the lid off.
Some seeds sprout even if the soil remains completely dry.
Ticket prices go up every spring even if the theatre is half empty.
His old knee aches even when the weather stays dry and mild.
The engine runs hot even if the coolant level looks normal.
Rents keep climbing even if wages remain flat for years.
Glaciers would shrink even if temperatures held steady from now on.
quiet: Sea levels would keep rising unless emissions stopped quite soon.
The soup cools within minutes once you take the lid off.
Most seeds sprout quickly when the soil is warm and moist.
Ticket prices go up every spring because the theatre is often full.
His old knee aches when the weather turns cold and wet.
The engine runs hot if the coolant level drops too low.
Rents keep climbing because wages have risen for years.
Glaciers shrink fastest when temperatures rise each summer.

predictions: 'even if/when' + steady-condition clauses reach about 0.2-0.4; plain conditional or causal versions stay under 0.1.
notes: Card is mixed (health, with, even, that, within); output suppresses 'without/normal/intact/unchanged'.
